status: written before any X1/X1b run was launched and before any M4X result was read (X2 validation was running; it is unaffected)
replaces: thresholds.bounded_entropy_adjusted.rule (used for the readings); thresholds.bounded_as_declared is unchanged
rule: From the 400k-decision checkpoint on, at every logged window t: let o_s = α_s·H_s·γ/(1−γ) and [lo_t, hi_t] = [min(0, min_s o_s), max(0, max_s o_s)] over the windows s from 400k decisions to t. The critic is bounded if q_max − hi_t ≤ 250, lo_t − q_min ≤ 250 and mean Q − hi_t ≤ +20 at every such window.
why: Subtracting the current window's offset assumes the critic already tracks the soft value of the current α and H. It does not: at the start α = 0.2 and H ≈ +1.3 give o ≈ +1,000 while a fresh critic reads ≈ 0, and when α rises the critic lags (M4U sac_demo_U_s0 at 1M decisions: o = −3,782, mean Q = −1,175), so the superseded rule calls lag a blow-up. The amended rule admits any value between 0 and the offsets observed since 400k, so only values that no observed α·H can justify fail. Entropy reaches its −2 target within about 150k decisions in every M4/M4U SAC run, so 400k (the first checkpoint after the initial one) excludes the start-up transient.
check_on_existing_runs: R SAC (3 runs) bounded; U SAC from scratch and SAC + demonstrations (6 runs) unbounded, as under the declared rule. Computed by m4x_report.py; runs before M4X lack per-window extremes, so their spread verdict uses max|Q| and can be 'undecided'.
